images.alt_en: The future: stem + σ + present endings (λύ-σ-ω), liquid and contract futures (μενῶ, καλῶ) and ἔσομαι
-μι verbs: reduplicated present stems δι-δω-/δι-δο-, τι-θη-/τι-θε-, ἱ-στη-/ἱ-στα-; long vowel in the singular, short in the plural
Genitive absolute: a noun + participle in the genitive, bracketed apart from the main clause, with 'when / since / although'
Attributive position (ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἀνήρ, ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἀγαθός) versus predicate position (ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθός, ἀγαθὸς ὁ ἀνήρ)
Supplementary participles: λανθάνω (unseen), τυγχάνω (happen to), φθάνω (get there first), φαίνομαι (plainly) as little scenes
ἵστημι: transitive ἔστησα 'I set up' (a hand placing a statue) and intransitive ἔστην / ἕστηκα 'I stood / I stand'
The four moods as four signposts: indicative (it is), subjunctive (let us / so that), optative (may it be / would), imperative (do!)
Purpose (ἵνα, ὅπως + subjunctive: an arrow to a target) and fear (φοβοῦμαι μή: a shadow ahead)
Direct speech in a bubble becoming reported speech three ways: ὅτι + indicative, accusative + infinitive, participle after verbs of knowing
Voice: active (A acts on B), middle (A acts for or on itself), passive (B is acted on, ὑπό + genitive for the agent)
Sequence of moods: after a primary verb the subjunctive, after a secondary (past) verb the optative
The perfect: a completed action with a lasting result (a door shut and still shut) on a timeline, beside aorist (point) and present (line)
A six-rung ladder of conditions from simple to contrary to fact, with the protasis and apodosis forms on each rung
Participle endings by tense and voice: -ων -ουσα -ον, -ας -ασα -αν, -ώς -υῖα -ός, -είς -εῖσα -έν, -μενος -μένη -μενον
Result with ὥστε: infinitive for a natural result, indicative for an actual one
Negatives: οὐ for facts and statements, μή for wishes, commands, conditions and purpose
Crasis (καὶ ἐγώ → κἀγώ, τὸ ὄνομα → τοὔνομα) and elision (ἀλλὰ ἐγώ → ἀλλ’ ἐγώ, ἐπὶ αὐτόν → ἐπ’ αὐτόν)
The dual: two oxen yoked together, with τὼ ἀδελφώ, τοῖν ἀδελφοῖν beside the singular and plural
Map of Attica in 431 BC: Athens and Piraeus inside the Long Walls, Acharnae, Eleusis, the Spartan army's route of invasion
Plan of the Pnyx: the speaker's platform (βῆμα), the seated citizens, the view to the Agora
The kleroterion, the allotment machine for jurors: slots for tickets and a tube of black and white balls
Reading strategy: find the verb, then the subject, then the objects; bracket participles and subordinate clauses

images.alt_en: Schematic map of Attica in three regions, city, coast and inland; each of Cleisthenes' ten tribes takes one third (trittys) from each region
How the democracy worked: the citizens, the Assembly, the Council of 500, the law courts and the officials, and what each did

Schematic map of south-east Sicily, 413 BC: the Athenian retreat from Syracuse, west towards the Akraian cliff, then south across the Kakyparis and Erineos to the Assinaros, where Nicias's army was destroyed
Schematic map of the Hellespont, 405 BC: the Athenian fleet beached at Aegospotami, Lysander's fleet at Lampsakos across the strait, Sestos, and the escape of the Paralos and Konon to the south-west
Schematic map of Cyrus's march of 401 BC from Sardis through Kelainai, Ikonion, Tarsos and Issos to Thapsakos on the Euphrates and down the river to Cunaxa near Babylon
